title: When the Verdict Breaks
premise: Retired detective Ulyana Kavanagh, now barely keeping their failing bookshop afloat, is stunned when a stranger's body is found wearing clothes stolen from their own closet — clothes that vanished the night of a verdict Ulyana helped deliver twenty years ago. The victim clutches a page from an old case ledger written in a cipher only Ulyana's late mentor could have devised, suggesting someone has been quietly settling scores tied to that long-ago trial. As the statute of limitations on the original crime ticks down, Ulyana must decode the ledger, confront the witness they once protected and betrayed, and face the truth that their perfect record was built on one case they closed too fast. In the end, Ulyana exposes the killer — the verdict's forgotten defendant, presumed dead — and chooses to surrender their own concealed role in the old miscarriage, trading their reputation for belonging to the truth at last.
about_author: K. M. Winterbourne is a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing other people's confessions before writing mysteries of their own. They live above a secondhand bookshop in a coastal town where everyone remembers everything.

chapters.title: The Clothes in the Closet
chapters.summary: Ulyana Kavanagh, POV. Opening in the failing bookshop, Ulyana discovers three garments missing from their closet — the same clothes later found on a corpse by the harbor. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the past knocking on a door Ulyana thought was locked.

chapters.title: A Stranger Wearing My Life
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Police confirm the dead man wore Ulyana's stolen clothes; the detective who arrives is Rhea Osei, once Ulyana's protégée. Ulyana hides the missing-clothes connection, guilt sharpening into resolve. Beat: shame disguised as cooperation.

chapters.title: The Ledger Page
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Among the victim's effects is a single ledger page in a cipher Ulyana recognizes as their late mentor Aldous Vane's invention. The page references 'the Verdict' and a date twenty years gone. Beat: grief rekindled into obsession.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Perfect Closures
chapters.summary: Rhea Osei, POV. Rhea investigates Ulyana's spotless record and finds one anomaly: the 2005 Harrow Verdict case, closed in nine days. She interviews the surviving witness, Marta Ilves, who flinches at Ulyana's name. Beat: doubt seeded in loyalty.

chapters.title: Marta Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana visits Marta Ilves, the protected witness whose testimony sealed the old verdict. Marta claims she never saw what she swore she saw — that Ulyana coached her. Beat: the ground tilting under a career built on certainty.

chapters.title: Cipher of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Working nights in the bookshop, Ulyana cracks the first layer: the ledger lists payments funneled through the courthouse itself. Someone inside the old trial was bought. Beat: cold clarity hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Bookshop as Bait
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana stages the remaining ledger pages visibly in the shop window, gambling the thief will return. A figure comes after closing but escapes, leaving behind a pressed lily — Marta's signature flower. Beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: What Rhea Kept From the File
chapters.summary: Rhea, POV. Rhea pulls the sealed autopsy addendum: the victim had been dead four days before being dressed, meaning someone preserved him. She begins suspecting Ulyana of staging the scene. Beat: trust fraying under procedure.

chapters.title: The Defendant Who Died
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Digging into the old case, Ulyana learns the convicted man, Tomas Reval, died in prison — or so records say. His body was cremated by a private firm owned by the trial's prosecutor. Beat: horror at how deep the rot runs.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Errors
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana finds Vane's hidden letter in a hollowed-out first edition: her mentor knew the verdict was bought and built the cipher ledger as insurance, then lost his nerve. He left it to Ulyana. Beat: betrayal and inheritance entwined.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Rhea, POV. Rhea learns the last charge connected to the old conspiracy expires in eleven days. Pressure descends from above to close the murder quickly — and quietly. Beat: institutional walls closing in.

chapters.title: The Witness Recants
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Marta publicly recants her twenty-year-old testimony, naming Ulyana as the one who shaped it. The town that loved the bookshop turns cold overnight. Beat: exile from the community Ulyana called home.

chapters.title: Second Layer of the Cipher
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Decoding deeper, Ulyana finds the ledger's final column blank except for one entry dated next week — a payment scheduled for the statute's eve. Someone plans to collect. Beat: racing the calendar.

chapters.title: The Prosecutor's Widow
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana confronts the prosecutor's widow, who reveals her husband was blackmailed by a judge — and that Tomas Reval's death certificate was signed by a doctor who never existed. Beat: the conspiracy has no bottom.

chapters.title: Rhea's Choice
chapters.summary: Rhea, POV. Ordered to arrest Ulyana on circumstantial evidence, Rhea instead shows Ulyana the file off the record. Two investigators, finally aligned. Beat: alliance forged in defiance of the institution.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Cremated
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Tracing the crematorium's records, Ulyana confirms Tomas Reval walked out alive under another name — and has been living in town for years, unremarkable, patient. Beat: the monster was always nearby.

chapters.title: Confession in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana admits to Rhea the full truth: they suppressed Marta's doubts to close the case and protect their record. Rhea must decide whether the confession ends their partnership. Beat: self-indictment as the price of integrity.

chapters.title: The Payment Date
chapters.summary: Rhea, POV. Surveillance of the courthouse on the statute's eve catches a clerk receiving cash — the last scheduled payoff. Following him leads to a boatyard warehouse. Beat: trap set, breath held.

chapters.title: Warehouse of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Rhea, alternating. Inside the warehouse they find Reval alive, along with evidence he murdered the courier to force the ledger into the open — his revenge engineered to expose everyone, including Ulyana. Beat: climax, all masks off.

chapters.title: When the Verdict Breaks
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Confronting Reval, Ulyana offers not arrest but acknowledgment: reading his exonerating ledger aloud as police arrive. Reval surrenders, undone by being believed at last. Beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Closing the Last Case
chapters.summary: Rhea, POV. Rhea files everything, including Ulyana's confession. Ulyana faces a misconduct board, loses their pension, and accepts it without defense. Beat: justice costing exactly what it should.

chapters.title: Belonging to the Truth
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Months later, the bookshop survives on new customers drawn by honesty rather than legend; Marta visits, tentative forgiveness offered. Ulyana shelves Vane's ledger openly behind the counter. Final beat: inheritance reclaimed, memory honored, home rebuilt on truth.
